Child agent-1 was delegated manual argparse behavior, wrote /output/lib/argparser.mjs, tested split and equals forms plus missing, invalid, unknown, missing-value, and help cases, then returned a completed parser summary.

The parent confirmed sample, negative, duplicate-key, and missing-argument behavior, launched three child writers, received all child results, ran integrated sample and edge checks, and closed with a passing local-check summary.

The single serial actor probed normal, duplicate-value, missing-argument, invalid-integer, same-key, and duplicate-assignment cases; wrote pyformat, bidict, argparse, and entry modules; corrected Map usage; verified samples and edge cases; and closed with a migration summary.

parallel.requirements: The parent recognized ESM .mjs output, exact console output, manual argv parsing, no external dependencies, black-box executable observation, and no Map-like implementation, but it introduced an unsupported assumption that values would be distinct.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent used AgentSwarm with three children: bidict library, argparse library, and test16 entry point. The parent retained final verification and delivery after receiving the aggregate child result.
parallel.implementation: The children wrote /output/test16.mjs, /output/lib/bidict.mjs, and /output/lib/argparser.mjs. The bidict module preserved insertion order and repr formatting but omitted duplicate-value errors because its brief said they were unnecessary.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The entry point imported the two delegated library modules and the parent later ran integrated commands after the swarm result. Artifact metadata confirms the three expected files were collected.
parallel.verification: Parallel verification covered the four samples, negative and zero values, duplicate-key overwrite, and missing required arguments, but it did not test duplicate values in construction or assignment.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official result remained false at 52/69. The directly evidenced parallel gap is the delegated bidict implementation's missing duplicate-value behavior; exact hidden failing test identities are not mounted.

serial.requirements: The serial actor kept the same global task constraints in one context and used the black-box executable to inspect both normal behavior and edge cases including duplicate values and argument errors.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial actor owned exploration, implementation, integration, verification, and final response itself, writing pyformat, bidict, argparse, and entry modules sequentially.
serial.implementation: The serial implementation added Python-style repr helpers, a bidict class with ValueDuplicationError for duplicate values, a manual argparse module, and a test16 entry point that catches duplicate-value errors.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial actor assembled all modules directly with local ESM imports and status metadata confirms four artifact files: test16.mjs, lib/argparse.mjs, lib/bidict.mjs, and lib/pyformat.mjs.
serial.verification: Serial verification compared sample cases, same-key overwrite, duplicate values in construction and assignment, missing arguments, and invalid integers against the executable.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite broader local edge coverage, the serial official result also failed at 52/69. Mounted records do not include per-case official failures, so remaining defects cannot be resolved from score alone.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the main ESM, .mjs, argv, output, and zero-dependency requirements but narrowed bidict behavior for the child by assuming distinct values.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and additionally probed duplicate-value behavior before implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The serial attempt covered a behavior class that the parallel parent removed from the delegated bidict scope.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split ownership into three child tasks for bidict, argparse, and entry code, with parent verification after the aggregate result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all ownership in the main actor, combining probing, implementation, correction, verification, and final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The split was productive but made the bidict child's scope depend on the parent's incomplete behavioral brief; serial avoided that handoff boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel supplied explicit file and import interfaces but the bidict child received a false input-domain statement that excluded duplicate-value behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained the duplicate-value observations in the same context that wrote the bidict implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The important interface was not a module import contract; it was task behavior context lost at delegation for the bidict child.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented a minimal bidict without duplicate-value rejection, a manual parser, and a simple entry script over those modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented repr helpers, strict bidict value uniqueness with ValueDuplicationError, parser behavior, and an entry script that catches the bidict error.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial's bidict implementation included an edge behavior missing from the parallel child implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All three children completed and the parent received the aggregate swarm result before running its final checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegated result lifecycle because the main actor performed all work directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No child result was trapped or missing; the important lifecycle issue is that the bidict result was complete for the narrowed brief but incomplete for the task.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote the shared /output tree; the entry child initially found only test16.mjs, but the parent later verified after all modules existed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and rewrote its modules sequentially in one workspace, including a bidict correction after noticing Map usage.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel shared workspace caused an early child check to be incomplete, but the parent closed the integration loop later, so no write-collision pattern is retained.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel local verification compared the four samples, negative and zero values, duplicate-key overwrite, and missing arguments, then declared completion.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial local verification covered the samples, same-key overwrite, duplicate values in construction and assignment, missing arguments, and invalid integers.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had broader edge verification for bidict uniqueness; parallel's final acceptance omitted that class.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished without timeout after 235.009 agent seconds, using three subagents and substantially more tokens than serial.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished without timeout after 147.768 agent seconds with no subagents and fewer total tokens.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel fan-out did not exhaust the budget or block closure; both runs closed normally and both failed official evaluation at the same aggregate score.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation records both runs as failed with 52 of 69 tests passed, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The concrete task-solving difference is that serial discovered and implemented duplicate-value bidict failures while parallel delegated the bidict module with that behavior excluded and then omitted duplicate-value acceptance checks.
parallel_contributors: The parent's bidict child brief asserted distinct values and no duplicate-error handling, narrowing the delegated implementation.
The parent verification suite covered samples, negatives, duplicate keys, and missing arguments but not duplicate values.
serial_contributors: The serial actor probed duplicate-value construction and assignment behavior against the executable.
The serial actor implemented and verified ValueDuplicationError behavior locally before final delivery.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial wrote an extra pyformat module and implemented more bidict edge behavior than the parallel bidict child.
Parallel and serial made different choices for argparse error program names during local checks; the mounted evaluator result does not expose which hidden cases failed.
evaluator_effects: Only aggregate official score records are mounted, so exact hidden failing testcase identities cannot be inspected from this isolated pair.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported process contrast without a unique official-failure root cause

candidates.reason: Parallel assigned implementation owners for bidict, argparse, and the entry file through the swarm; the defect is narrowed context, not absence of an implementer.
The parent retained integration and ran end-to-end checks after the child results, so integration was owned even though coverage was incomplete.
The entry file was explicitly delegated and the final artifact set was collected, so final assembly and placement were not ownerless.
The parent covered exploration, delegation, aggregate result consumption, integrated verification, and closure, so the end-to-end pipeline had an owner.
The parent performed a short behavior probe before delegation, but productive implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial gate with an adverse delay consequence.
Parallel did not run overlapping investigators as a separate first phase; it delegated implementation modules directly after limited parent exploration.
No indispensable implementation path was starved of workers or started too late; all delegated pieces completed and the specific failure is the bidict brief content.
The run used only three children, did not time out, and still had time for parent verification; there is no collective breadth or retry exhaustion event.
Each child received a small module-level scope and completed; the bidict child's problem was missing scope content, not an overbroad assignment.

The parent delegated the bidict module with a false distinct-values assumption and no duplicate-error scope despite the global requirement to match executable behavior; the child followed that narrowed brief.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parallel bidict module omitted duplicate-value rejection and the parent accepted it after a verification set that never exercised duplicate values.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent did run integrated checks; the earlier delegated brief explains why the duplicate-value behavior was absent, and hidden evaluator failure alone cannot establish unsupported global completion.

candidates.reason: The delegated modules had explicit file paths and import interfaces, and no independently produced components were observably incompatible at integration time.
There is no known finding that was transferred and then lost; the duplicate-value behavior was omitted from the initial bidict child brief.
The aggregate swarm result was lengthy but the parent consumed it enough to run integrated checks; no result was unusable because of handoff volume.
No receiver acted on a superseded workspace or requirement state; the important false statement was present from the first bidict delegation.
No incompatible child reports or contracts reached the parent and remained unresolved; the child reports were mutually compatible for the narrowed implementation.
The parent made a completion statement after integrated local checks; no parent-visible integrated mismatch is shown before closure, and evaluator status alone cannot create this label.
The parallel trajectory has no replacement child or retry that repeated work without inherited findings or current-file state.

candidates.reason: All three children completed normally; no active child was explicitly stopped or cancelled before needed work finalized.
The required files were written and collected; there was no complete candidate left unpromoted or unplaced before closure.
The entry child's early syntax-only check happened before sibling modules existed, but the parent later ran integrated checks after all child results arrived.
The parent received the completed implementation child results and ran the assembled entry point from the shared output tree.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that failed to return to the parent; verification was parent-run after implementation results.
No required child failed or was cancelled; the entry child reported lack of sibling modules for end-to-end testing and the parent later took over integrated checks.
The parent received and used the completed swarm result before running final integrated verification, so no completed child result was ignored.
The parent did not wait until timeout or a deadline without inspecting available progress; the session completed normally and proceeded after child completion.
Children wrote different files with intended modular roles; no competing implementation paths claimed the same behavior or build ownership.
No two live parallel agents edited the same file or had to reconcile concurrent same-file edits.
No agent replaced a non-entry source file produced or actively owned by another agent.
The entry deliverable was assigned to and written by the entry child; no other actor overwrote it while it was owned or used.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replacing multiple current outputs in the final workspace.
The children shared /output and the entry child observed missing sibling modules early, but the parent later verified the assembled tree; no unstable final state or provenance problem resulted.
No generated temporary file, cache, fixture, tool, or auxiliary artifact from one concurrent actor was consumed by another as stable reference input.

retained_patterns.reason: The parent delegated the bidict module with a narrowed distinct-values-only assumption even though the task required black-box behavioral equivalence. The child implemented to that narrowed brief, and the parent did not exercise duplicate-value cases before final delivery.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parallel deliverable lacked duplicate-value bidict failure behavior and closed after local checks that could not reveal that omission.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The parent did perform integrated post-swarm checks; the direct corrective boundary is the initial bidict child brief, not final acceptance based only on hidden evaluator failure.
